reviews.comment: Overall, this is a well-organized introduction to compressed sensing. It conveys important ideas useful beyond the subject itself. Prof. Foucart is very dedicated—his lectures are clear, he answers questions thoroughly, and he even grades the homework himself. The course can be challenging without a strong math background, but it is very rewarding.

Well the professor is a good person, no doubt about that. But that's about the only good thing I will say in this review. The lectures are difficult, the homework is even more so. The exams fortunately were tame compared to the homework. Starting the class without a good grasp of college level algebra, linear algebra and calculus is a mistake.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You MUST go to class, do the homework, go over any questions you missed, and study incredibly hard for the tests. If you weren't great at linear algebra, spend some time reviewing the concepts beforehand. Everything that he assigns will take more than a basic understanding to complete. Review your midterm when studying for the final.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Foucart is incredibly smart, but his lectures are hard to follow and do not help on the tests. I have a 4.0 and I struggled to make a C throughout the semester. Our test average was never above a 45. This class seriously made me consider dropping my major.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Foucart is a brilliant professor. He's incredibly smart and can answer pretty much all questions on the fly in lectures. From a mathematics perspective, his lectures are rigorous and clean. Work hard not to get behind, though, as he expects you have a good grasp over stuff that he already covered. Tests are challenging, expect to be daunted.
